turns.user: why does my plan put protein in every single meal? can't I just have a big steak at dinner and be done
turns.reply:
Spreading your protein across the day actually helps your body build and retain muscle much better than eating it all in one sitting. 

Your body can only trigger muscle protein synthesis — the process that repairs and builds muscle tissue — so many times a day, and it needs a solid hit of protein (usually 25–40g) each time to get that signal going. If you dump all 130g of your daily target into dinner, your body will use what it needs for repair in that window, but the rest gets burned for energy rather than helping your muscles recover throughout the day.

Having protein at breakfast and lunch keeps that repair signal turning on every few hours, which keeps you full longer and helps with fat loss.

That said, your targets are total daily goals, not strict rules. If you have a lighter protein lunch and a massive steak for dinner once in a while, it won't ruin your progress — the total at the end of the day still matters most. 

Would you like to adjust how your protein is split across your meals, or keep it balanced like it is?
